text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD

- The Netherlands presents its 1997 budge and will almost certainly qualify for European economic and monetary union in 1998, paper says. "The Netherlands will pass the EMU with this budget," says finance minister Gerrit Zalm.
Main points of budget:
- Budget deficit to fall to 2.2 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 from 2.6 percent this year.
- Government debt as a percentage of GDP will fall by 2.5 percentage points to 76.2 percent.
- Total government spending will rise to 155 billion guilders in 1997 from 149.8 billion this year.
- Government borrowing requirement will be an estimated 33.5 billion guilders in 1997.
- Income tax and social security contributions in first tax bracket will be cut by 0.2 percent to 37.3 percent, the second tax bracket will be extrended by 3,350 guilders.
- The tax and social security premium will fall by one billion guilders.
- Around 100,000 new jobs expected to be created.
- Excise duty on cigarettes and tobacco to rise 50 guilder cents per packet, ordinary petrol to rise 15 guilder cents a litre and diesel five cents a litre.
Non-budget news:

- Anglo-Dutch software developer CMG forecasts stronger turnover growth than the 10-15 percent predicted for the information technology market as a whole. Company announces first half net jumps 34 percent to 18.2 million guilders.
- Reed Elsevier again seeking to take over exhibition and conference organiser Blenhiem Group. Press reports put potential cost of Blenheim at 500 million sterling.
VOLKSKRANT
- Nedlloyd to raise 200 million guilders from the sale of its half of North Sea Ferries to P&O, resulting in a 20 million guilder book profit.
- Albert Heijn, Vroom and Dreesman and Shell drop plan to offer electronic consumer "smart cards", because of costs.
DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet proposes to make two billion guilders available to tackle problem traffic queues in the Randstadt conurbation.

- National insurance patients must from 1997 pay 20 percent of the costs of their medical treatment up to a maximum of 200 guilders a year. Visits to general practitioners, dentists and obstetric care will be exempt.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Stork's Fokker Aviation wins contracts to carry out work on Boeing 737's that will go beyond current "garage" work, making it a "support" for the U.S. firm in Europe.
- Transport minister Anne-Marie Jorritsma demands that companies who want to compete with rail firm NS must also take on unprofitable lines in any takeover deal.
